I'll help you find how text positions are calculated for NPCs and Alfred in the game. Let me search for relevant code in your workspace. Now let me search for the specific text display and positioning code: Now let me search specifically for how the text position is calculated relative to the speaker: Now let me look for documentation specifically about text/dialogue positioning: Let me search more specifically for text positioning code: Based on my analysis of the game's code and documentation, here's how text position is calculated for both NPCs and Alfred:

## Text Position Calculation

### Y Position Formula (Vertical Placement)

The text bubble Y position is calculated in the `display_talk_animation_and_wait` function at **address 0x000193a8**:

```c
// Calculate Y position - places bubble ABOVE the character's head
if ((speaker_y_position - (0x66 - scaling_offset)) < 0x3C) {
    bubble_y = 1;  // Clamp to near top if too high
}
else {
    bubble_y = speaker_y_position - ((0x66 - scaling_offset) + bubble_height);
}
```

**Where:**
- `speaker_y_position` = Character's Y coordinate (feet position)
- `0x66` (102 decimal) = Character sprite height in pixels
- `scaling_offset` = Vertical scaling adjustment based on perspective/depth
- `bubble_height` = Height of the rendered text bubble
- `0x3C` (60 decimal) = Minimum Y threshold to prevent going off-screen

**The formula positions the bubble ABOVE the character by:**
1. Starting at the character's feet position
2. Subtracting the character height (adjusted for scaling)
3. Subtracting the bubble height
4. Clamping to a minimum of Y=1 if result would be < 60

### X Position Formula (Horizontal Centering)

```c
// Center bubble horizontally on character
bubble_x = speaker_x_position - (bubble_width / 2);

// Clamp to screen bounds (640 pixels wide)
if (speaker_x_position < bubble_width/2) {
    bubble_x = 0;
}
if (639 - speaker_x_position < bubble_width/2) {
    bubble_x = 639 - bubble_width;
}
```

### NPC vs Alfred: **Same Calculation**

Both NPCs and Alfred use the **identical positioning algorithm**. The difference is:
- **Alfred**: Uses `alfred_y_position` and `alfred_scale_y` variables
- **NPCs**: The same function is called with the NPC sprite's Y position and scaling values

The text bubble is **always positioned relative to the speaker's sprite position**, regardless of whether it's Alfred or an NPC.

### Related Functions

- **`display_text_description` (0x0001a298)**: Word-wraps text, calculates bubble dimensions
- **`trigger_dialog_or_action` (0x0001a683)**: Renders text into the bubble buffer
- **`display_talk_animation_and_wait` (0x000193a8)**: **Calculates screen position** and displays bubble with animation
- **`display_sprite_talk_animation` (0x00019592)**: Similar positioning for NPC dialogue

The bubble gets inserted into the render queue with Z-depth=1, ensuring it renders on top of other sprites.

max_scan:\n                            p1 = pair12[pos + j + 1]\n                            p2 = pair12[pos + j + 2]\n                            print(f\"[{j:04X}] 0xF8 {p1:02X} {p2:02X} - ACTION TRIGGER\")\n                            j += 2\n                        elif b == 0xFA:\n                            print(f\"[{j:04X}] 0xFA - DISABLE CHOICE\")\n                        \n                        j += 1\n            \n            i += 1\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    analyze_first_choice()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

{
  "invocationMessage": "Using \"Replace String in File\"",
  "isConfirmed": {
    "type": 1
  },
  "content": "&#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\n## Critical Structure Discoveries\n\n### Text Line Indices\n\n**Every dialogue line has a sequential text line index** that starts after the descriptions:\n\n- Room with 10 descriptions (sprites + hotspots) → Conversation lines start at index 10\n- Each line (NPC speech, ALFRED choice, NPC response) gets its own sequential index\n- Format: &#96;0x08 [speaker_id] [text_line_index] 0x00 [text] 0xFD&#96;\n\n**Example from Room 2:**\n- 10 descriptions (indices 0-9)\n- First NPC line: index 10 (0x0A)\n- First ALFRED choice: index 11 (0x0B)\n- NPC response: index 12 (0x0C)\n- And so on...\n\nThis index is stored in the conversation data and helps track which lines have been displayed.\n\n### Conversation Roots and Branch Termination\n\n**Conversations can have multiple \"roots\" (entry points):**\n\n1. **0xF4 (END_CONVERSATION)**:\n   - Completely ends the current branch\n   - **DISABLES the current conversation root**\n   - When player talks again, this root will NOT appear\n   - Jumps to the next available root (if any)\n   - **Use case**: Choices that should be removed after selection\n\n2. **0xF7 (END_BRANCH)**:\n   - Ends the current branch\n   - **Does NOT disable anything**\n   - Immediately continues to the next conversation root\n   - **Use case**: Natural conversation flow between related topics\n\n**Real Example from Room 2:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nROOT 1: NPC asks \"Te apetece pasar un buen rato?\"\n  ├─ Choice \"No se, ¿Cuanto cobras?\" → negotiations → eventually 0xF7\n  └─ Choice \"No puedo. Estoy buscando a una princesa\" → NPC insults → 0xF4 (DISABLES this choice)\n\n(After 0xF7 or if ROOT 1 disabled)\nROOT 2: NPC asks \"¿Has conseguido los condones?\"\n  ├─ Choice \"Estoy en ello\" → NPC responds → 0xF4\n  └─ Choice \"No los hay de mi tamaño\" → Long response → 0xF4\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Action Triggers (0xF8)\n\nThe &#96;0xF8&#96; byte triggers game state changes:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n[0xF8] [parameter1] [parameter2]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Common uses:**\n- Mark choices as disabled/completed\n- Set game flags\n- Trigger events or animations\n- Modify inventory\n- Check conditions\n\n**Example from Room 2:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n0xF8 0x48 0x01  // After \"No vuelvas sin ellos\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis likely sets a flag or marks that the player needs to find condons.\n\n### Complete Byte Sequence Structure\n\n**Speaker line:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n[0xFC 0x41]        // Segment separator (optional, between segments)\n[0x08]             // Speaker marker\n[speaker_id]       // 0x0D = ALFRED, 0x20 = NPC, others = specific NPCs\n[text_line_index]  // Sequential from after descriptions\n[0x00]             // Always zero\n[...text bytes...] // Actual text content\n[0xFD]             // End of text\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Choice line:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n[0xFB or 0xF1]     // Dialogue marker\n[choice_index]     // Groups related choices (1-255)\n[0x08]             // Speaker marker\n[speaker_id]       // Usually 0x0D for ALFRED\n[text_line_index]  // Sequential index\n[0x00]             // Always zero\n[...text bytes...] // Choice text\n[0xFD]             // End of text\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Important**: The &#96;0x00&#96; byte after text_line_index is NOT part of the text - your parser was incorrectly reading it as part of the text content.\n\n## Conversation Data Format\n\nEach conversation entry in pair 12:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n",
  "textEditContent": "## Critical Structure Discoveries\n\n### Text Line Indices\n\n**Every dialogue line has a sequential text line index** that starts after the descriptions:\n\n- Room with 10 descriptions (sprites + hotspots) → Conversation lines start at index 10\n- Each line (NPC speech, ALFRED choice, NPC response) gets its own sequential index\n- Format: &#96;0x08 [speaker_id] [text_line_index] 0x00 [text] 0xFD&#96;\n\n**Example from Room 2:**\n- 10 descriptions (indices 0-9)\n- First NPC line: index 10 (0x0A)\n- First ALFRED choice: index 11 (0x0B)\n- NPC response: index 12 (0x0C)\n- And so on...\n\nThis index is stored in the conversation data and helps track which lines have been displayed.\n\n### Conversation Roots and Branch Termination\n\n**Conversations can have multiple \"roots\" (entry points):**\n\n1. **0xF4 (END_CONVERSATION)**:\n   - Completely ends the current branch\n   - **DISABLES the current conversation root**\n   - When player talks again, this root will NOT appear\n   - Jumps to the next available root (if any)\n   - **Use case**: Choices that should be removed after selection\n\n2. **0xF7 (END_BRANCH)**:\n   - Ends the current branch\n   - **Does NOT disable anything**\n   - Immediately continues to the next conversation root\n   - **Use case**: Natural conversation flow between related topics\n\n**Real Example from Room 2:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nROOT 1: NPC asks \"Te apetece pasar un buen rato?\"\n  ├─ Choice \"No se, ¿Cuanto cobras?\" → negotiations → eventually 0xF7\n  └─ Choice \"No puedo.
